title: How the brain separates sounds
review_question: What are the neural mechanisms underlying Auditory Scene Analysis (ASA), particularly auditory streaming and concurrent sound segregation, and how does attention influence these processes?
inclusion_exclusion_criteria: Not explicitly defined, typical for a narrative review synthesizing research on auditory scene analysis.

findings.antecedent: streaming cues (e.g., frequency difference, presentation rate)
findings.consequent: neural responses in primary auditory cortex and EEG wave components (latency <200ms)
findings.source: Abstract
findings.quote: Listeners' sensitivity to streaming cues can be captured in the responses of neurons in the primary auditory cortex, and in EEG wave components with a short latency (<200ms).

findings.source: Abstract
findings.quote: However, streaming can be strongly affected by attention, suggesting that this early processing either receives input from non-auditory areas, or feeds into processes that do.

findings.consequent: tendency to hear two auditory streams (build-up effect)

findings.antecedent: rare deviant sound in a sequence of standards
findings.source: EEG
findings.quote: The MMN is observed when a rare deviant sound... is presented in a sequence of otherwise identical 'standards'. It takes the form of a negative wave, with a latency of 150-200 ms...

findings.consequent: MMN to deviant tones in a streaming context
findings.source: EEG
findings.quote: They observed an MMN when the stimulus onset asynchrony (SOA) between successive tones was 100 ms, at which behavioral experiments suggest that streaming should occur.

findings.source: EEG
findings.quote: MMN to deviants in some paradigms can be measured in the absence of attention... more recent evidence shows that the MMN can be affected by attention.

findings.source: EEG
findings.quote: They used an SOA of 500 ms and observed an MMN only when subjects were attending to the tones, and concluded that, for this stimulus, attention did indeed modulate streaming.

findings.consequent: serial recall of visually presented letters
findings.source: Effects of streaming on competing tasks
findings.quote: Recall can be disrupted by sound sequences that subjects are instructed to ignore, provided that the sounds change over time.

findings.source: Effects of streaming on competing tasks
findings.quote: when two tones were presented in an alternating sequence, recall was disrupted if the tones were heard as a single stream, but not if they were heard as two separate streams.

findings.source: Effects of streaming on competing tasks
findings.quote: when subjects were instructed to ignore the sounds, streaming still occurred, and disrupted recall, but the amount of streaming was less than when subjects were attending to the sounds.

findings.antecedent: initial inattention to sound sequence followed by later attention
findings.source: Manipulating attention during the build-up of streaming
findings.quote: when subjects initially ignored a sequence and then started making streaming judgements, the amount of streaming reported is much less than if they were attending all along.

findings.source: Manipulating attention during the build-up of streaming
findings.quote: streaming is not an automatic process that builds up regardless of attention, but that attention is required for the build-up to occur.

findings.antecedent: unilateral neglect (right hemisphere damage) + sound presented to left ear
findings.source: Non-auditory areas and auditory streaming
findings.quote: These same subjects showed reduced streaming for sounds presented to their left ear, compared with when the sounds were presented to their right ear or to either ear of controls.

findings.antecedent: mistuning of one component from a harmonic complex
findings.consequent: specific neural response patterns (e.g., in inferior colliculus, IC)
findings.source: Neural and cognitive bases of ASA: concurrent sound segregation
findings.quote: a particular type of response occurs in a predictable way for mistuning with a wide range of stimuli, and that it does not occur for stimuli which are not mistuned.

findings.antecedent: mistuning of a component in a harmonic complex
findings.source: Neural and cognitive bases of ASA: concurrent sound segregation
findings.quote: Alain and his colleagues... have observed responses to a sequence of complex tones, which could be either perfectly harmonic or have one partial mistuned... (ORN).

findings.source: Neural and cognitive bases of ASA: concurrent sound segregation
findings.quote: The size of the ORN increased monotonically with the amount of mistuning, in a manner similar to the increase in the tendency of listeners to report hearing two sound sources.

findings.source: Neural and cognitive bases of ASA: concurrent sound segregation
findings.quote: it would therefore be reassuring to know that other manipulations, which did not result in the percept of two sound sources, did not produce an ORN.

findings.source: Neural and cognitive bases of ASA: concurrent sound segregation
findings.quote: an earlier component, with a latency of around 30 ms, which increases monotonically with increases in mistuning, but which also differs between perfectly harmonic complexes.

synthesis_conclusions: Auditory Scene Analysis (ASA) involves grouping simultaneous frequency components into auditory objects and organizing sequential sounds into streams.
Neural mechanisms for simultaneous sound segregation are still in their infancy, with some evidence for neural responses to mistuning but a challenge to link these to perceived segregation.
Auditory streaming has shown more progress, with single-cell responses in primary auditory cortex mimicking effects of frequency separation and presentation rate.
Auditory streaming can occur at peripheral stages but is also strongly affected by attention, suggesting more central processing and interaction with cognitive functions.

The multiplicity of factors influencing streaming makes it unlikely to pinpoint streaming to a single neural locus; a more fruitful approach is to characterize the interaction of processes like selectivity, adaptation, and attention.
evidence_gaps: The earliest stage of processing at which the effects of frequency difference, repetition rate, and the build-up of streaming can be observed is unknown.
The stage in the auditory pathway where attention affects neural correlates of streaming, and whether these effects are confined to auditory processing areas, is unclear.
Evidence for the effect of attention on simultaneous sound segregation is lacking, raising questions about its automaticity or current methodological limitations.
It is unclear whether the reduced streaming reported after initial inattention is due to a lack of build-up or a 'reset' of streaming by switching attention.
limitations: The neural mechanisms underlying simultaneous sound segregation are largely unknown, and it is challenging to link neural responses to the perception of segregated components.
It is difficult to definitively ascertain if MMN responses occur truly outside the focus of attention, as subjects might 'sneak a little listen'.
The multiplicity of factors influencing streaming makes it unlikely to 'pin down' streaming to a specific neural locus.

environmental_features: sequences of pure tones or complex tones with varying frequency differences and presentation rates

theory_commitments.specific_claim: The auditory system organizes complex sound mixtures into separate perceptual streams corresponding to distinct sound sources based on acoustic cues.

mechanism_chain.description: Causal mechanism linking acoustic streaming cues to early cortical neural responses and EEG components, reflecting the brain's process of separating sounds.
